text:
Between forty and fifty Hong-
kong strikers have been injured,
some seriously, at a mock trial of
an alleged spy and "traitor" at
Tung Yuen, near the second bund,
Canton, writes the "China Mail"
correspondent.

label: text
text: A few days ago a Chinese who bore the appearance of the average workman was surrounded by a strike picket and accused of being a spy. It is believed that the unfortunate man is a striker himself but he had, apparently, incurred the enmity of a strike official. At any rate, he was roughly handled and subsequently marched off to the Strike Executive headquarters. A trial was ordered and was held, subsequently, close to a partly completed building which was propped up by beams.

label: text
text: Before the trial started, a large crowd of idlers had assembled to watch the fun. To obtain vantage points some of them entered the building in course of erection. Their weight was such that a collapse ensued, throwing the “court” into confusion.

label: text
text: Of those injured the majority were seamen. The "prisoner's trial has yet to come off.

label: text
text: A sign of the more hopeful outlook in the strike situation was the presence of a more varied class of workers at the Police Station this morning.

label: text
text: The Chief Detectiveive Inspector (Mr. Grant) supplied 1,000 cosies this morning against orders in hand from the various concerns requiring labour. All the orders were filled, and Mr. Grant was in a position to supply 500 more if necessary from the cooiles waiting on the compound for work.

label: text
text: A large number of seamen also applied for work. These included 60 sailors, a number of engineers, and coxswains. The engineers secured ready employment, as also some of the sailors and coxswains. Six coxswains, all holding certificates for steam launch work, attended this morning for work. They were being detained at the office pending the decision of the "Star" Ferry Company who had been communicated with as regards employment for these men.

label: text
text: The Canton Seamen's Union has opened a branch in Tientsin city and, attempted to bring out the seamen on foreign boats.

label: text
text: They are distributing the usual propaganda but the seamen refused to strike.

label: text
text: It is understood the British Consult is protesting to the authorities against intimidation attempts.

label: text
text: Mr. Patrick, Chief Officer of the Hop Sang, which vessel was at the time at Kowloon Dockes, sustained injuries to his buck and wrist as a result of a fall into the hold yester-day.

label: text
text: Some of the staff of the Hongkong and Whampoa Dock were near at the time, and with their assistance Mr. Patrick was conveyed from the hold, and after temporary first aid had been rendered, the injured officer was taken by launch to the French Hospital at Causeway Bay.

label: text
text: The rainfall for the month of June at the Botanical Gardens was 24ins. 74 on 21 days, at the Matilda Hospital, Mount Kellett, was 21ins. 11 on 21 days, and at the Police Station, Taipo, it was 21ins. 17 on 18 days. The lowest barometer reading at sea level was 29ins. 582 at 18h on the 6th.

text: Rescue work in connection with the disaster which attended the collapse of houses in the Western part of the City was continued during the whole of last night with over 100 workers.

label: text
text: Latest figures of casualties are: dead 34; injured and in hospital 18, of whom 4 have been discharged.

label: text
text: It is estimated that at least 50 persons are buried in the ruins on which work was still proceeding this morning. House No. 16, adjoining the scene of the disaster and part of which was involved has had to be propped up as it was giving signs of becoming dangerous to the rescue party.

label: text
text: Floods which in some cases immersed all but the roofs of houses, and in others led to their entire collapse, occurred yesterday at Kowloon Tong, as a result of the heavy rains and the prevention of the escape of huge volumes of water from an overflowing pond by the barrier made by the proposed new road. Many of the inhabitants had to be rescued through the roofs by means of rafts and lifelines.

label: text
text: There were no casualties other than the effects of emersion on a woman and two children who were taken to the Kwong Wah Hospital and injury sustained to, his foot by a fireman as he swam from one house to another.

label: text
text: If it had not been for the good work of helpers on the spot (including Europeans), and the firemen, many would undoubtedly have been drowned. Hundreds were rendered homeless and were to be observed yesterday making their way. from the village to other parts with what they were able to rescue of their belongings. text: Moscow, July 16.—General Hsu has arrived here and is to stay ten days.—Reuter.

label: text
text: As predicted in the "China Mail" a few days ago the shortage of eggs in the Colony has now become acute.

label: text
text: Upon enquiry at the office of the Food Controller, Mr. N. L. Smith, the “China Mail” was informed that the Dairy Farm had no eggs in cold storage. The shortage was due, said Mr. Smith, to the disturbed conditions in neighbouring parts of China, supplies in the ordinary way coming chiefly from Tientsin and Swatow.

label: text
text: Arrangements were being made to meet the shortage and he himself, said Mr. Smith, was in communication with Swatow and by an indirect means hoped to get supplies in the near future. He understood that the Dairy Farm were in communication with Manila.

label: text
text: If the arrangements made with Swatow were fulfilled, there might be little change in the price of eggs, said Mr. Smith, but possibly the Manila eggs would be more.

label: text
text: As regarded the general food situation, everything was functioning almost normally, but there was likely to be a falling off in the supply of live stock. Steps had already been taken to meet this but in order that there might be consistency in the supplies, less killing was to be carried out until stocks were replenished.

label: text
text: Charles Maurras, editor of the "Action Francaise," has been sentenced to two years' imprisonment or, in default, to be fined 1,000 francs, on a charge of publicating an open letter declaring if the Minister of the Interior Schrameck attempted to disarm members of the League Action Francaise without disarming the Communists, he will kill him "like a dog."

text: Basing the decision on a presumption of undue influence, the Probate Court refused to admit probate for McClintock's will by which the estate passes to Shepherd.

text: In a film now being shown of the King and Queen's visit to Treasure Island, at Wembley, little Joan Molison, who was born in Yokohama and lost some of her relatives during the earthquake, is seen in the miniature railway car seated opposite his Majesty holding an animated conversation.

label: text
text: Another good show was put up by the younger set of amateurs in the Lord's cricket match with the professionals. Jack Hobbs has made another century and Percy Holmes of Yorkshire has been honoured by being picked for the big match. After his record score on the ground it was a foregone conclusion that he would be chosen. Incidentally several other Yorkshiremen did well.

label: text
text: In the county results it will be seen that Yorkshire—probably missing their stalwarts—dropped points for the second time this season, not being able to press home an advantage. Kent made a glorious struggle and won after following on. Glamorgan record their first win in the championship this year and both Worcester and Lancashire won away.

text: The discovery of a new local anesthetic, possessing all the virtues of cocaine but none of its perils, was announced at the annual meeting of the British Medical Association at Bath at which the Dominions, India, Ceylon and Hongkong were represented.

label: text
text: The discovery was made by a Cambridge doctor named Copeland who was awarded the memorial scholarship to the value of £200.
